title: Comparison of in vivo measurements from two pressure measurement systems for assessing interface pressure under lymphatic compression devices
summary:
In the treatment of lymphedema, wearing compression garments is an important part of therapy. Pressure measurement systems are used to verify that these compression garments apply the correct pressure to the affected tissue. The device most commonly used to date (PicoPress) provides reliable measurements but is complex to use. A more user-friendly device (Juzo Pressure Monitor) is intended to simplify pressure measurement and thus make it easier to use. 
Twenty-eight patients with lower-leg lymphedema are participating in the study. Both measuring devices are applied simultaneously on the lower leg while the compression system is in place. Measurements are taken in various body positions as well as during specific movements. The readings from both devices are then compared and statistically analyzed.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Unilateral or bilateral lymphedema of the extremities
- Stage II or III
- Currently undergoing compression therapy
- Trained in the use of adjustable compression wraps
- Sufficient manual and sensory function to use adjustable compression wraps
- Sufficient verbal comprehension and cognitive ability to participate in the study
- Willingness to participate in the study and provide informed consent
Exclusion criteria:
- Significant changes in circumference or anatomical deviations from the approximate physiological circumference at measurement point B1 at the junction of the Achilles tendon and the gastrocnemius muscle due to lymphedema
- Contraindications or intolerance to compression therapy
